after: ## Which unit goes with which quantity
alt: A table pairing each quantity with its unit: mass in kilograms (kg), energy and work done in joules (J), distance and height in metres (m), speed in m/s, g in m/s² (the same as N/kg), force in newtons (N), time in seconds (s), power in watts (W), and efficiency with no unit. W can mean work done or watt, and m can mean mass or metre.
caption: Each quantity has one unit; W and m each have two meanings.

alt: Unit links: 1 J = 1 N × 1 m; 1 W = 1 J / 1 s; 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s². For kinetic energy, kg × (m/s)² = kg m²/s² = N m = J; for gravitational potential energy, kg × m/s² × m = N × m = J. Both stores are in joules.
caption: Every Topic 4 unit can be built from the others, so units can be checked.

alt: Prefix conversions: 250 mJ = 0.25 J, 3.5 kJ = 3500 J, 2.2 kW = 2200 W, 1.8 MJ = 1.8 × 10⁶ J. Other conversions: 500 g ÷ 1000 = 0.500 kg, 45 cm ÷ 100 = 0.45 m, minutes × 60 and hours × 3600 give seconds, and 72 km/h ÷ 3.6 = 20 m/s.
caption: Grams, centimetres, minutes, km/h and prefixed units all convert before substituting.

alt: A 1200 kg car at 72 km/h: v = 72 / 3.6 = 20 m/s, so KE = 0.5 × 1200 × 20² = 240 000 J = 240 kJ. Substituting 72 directly gives 3 110 400 J, almost thirteen times too big, shown by bars drawn to scale.
caption: Convert km/h to m/s before squaring, or the error is squared too.

alt: A lift motor with useful power 4.5 kW = 4500 W runs for 2.0 × 60 = 120 s, transferring 540 000 J = 0.54 MJ. A 75 kg climber gains 75 × 10 × 300 = 225 000 J of GPE in 1500 s, an average power of 150 W.
caption: Convert kW to W and minutes to seconds on separate lines first.

alt: Rearranging KE = ½mv²: v = √(2 × KE / m) has units √(J/kg) = √(m²/s²) = m/s, a speed, while the wrong v = √(KE × m / 2) gives kg m/s. J ÷ s = W and W × s = J, so a 2 kW heater transfers 2 kJ each second; efficiency is J ÷ J and has no unit.
caption: If the units of a rearranged equation do not give the right quantity, it is wrong.
